matchups.recap: Rob got absolutely skull-fucked this week, limping across the finish line with 72.1 points like a three-legged dog in a track meet. Down by 30.4, this wasn't even a loss—it was a goddamn mercy killing. Whatever dogshit lineup decisions Rob made this week, they were so catastrophically bad that Rilind didn't even need to try; he just showed up and watched Rob's season go up in flames. Next time Rob wants to compete, he should try actually checking his roster before kickoff instead of punting the entire week like he's playing fantasy football on a fucking flip phone.

Adam got absolutely fucked 128.7 to 86.6—a 42-point beatdown that makes you wonder if he accidentally set his lineup on a fucking potato. Jetmir and Peter didn't even need to break a sweat; they could've left the bench empty and still won by three TDs. Adam's team played like it was on life support, and somebody definitely pulled the plug before halftime.

Rinor got absolutely obliterated 155.5 to 115.5—a 40-point ass-kicking that makes you wonder if he even showed up to the draft sober or just let his dog autodraft the whole thing. This wasn't a loss, it was a public execution; Ilir didn't just beat you, he curb-stomped your entire roster into the dirt and pissed on it for good measure. At this point Rinor should've just left his lineup blank because whatever the fuck he put out there clearly wasn't the answer.

Faton just got absolutely demolished by his own flesh and blood, losing by over 40 points—that's a family dinner conversation that's gonna sting for months. Flamur's gonna be bringing this up every single holiday until the end of time, and honestly, Faton deserves it for showing up with a lineup that looked like he drafted it while blackout drunk. Better luck next year, little bro—or wherever you fall in the Muriqi pecking order, because it sure as hell isn't at the top anymore.

Veton got absolutely skull-fucked by 32 points this week, and honestly, that's generous—watching his lineup was like watching someone try to perform surgery with a baseball bat. His team played dead on arrival, and Arben didn't even need to bring his A-game to send him back to the drawing board. Veton's going to need therapy, not a trade, to recover from this ass-kicking.

Ben got absolutely fucking obliterated by 78 points—that's not a loss, that's a mercy killing. You scored 87.6 points in what I assume was a full PPR league with 14 bench spots, which means somewhere on your roster was a guy who got negative points and you still started him. Nori didn't just beat you, he made you question every single personnel decision you've made since the draft, and frankly, you should be.

matchups.preview: Rob's already found creative ways to lose one game, so naturally he's about to get cute with his lineup and bench his best player against Adam, who'll somehow still manage to fuck up his own team badly enough that it won't matter—except Rob will find a way to lose anyway because that's just what Rob does.

Rinor's already down 0-1 and now has to face his own family across the matchup—nothing says "pass the potatoes at Thanksgiving" like getting embarrassed by another Ahmetaj. Rilind's sitting pretty at 1-0 and about to remind Rinor exactly why the family group chat is gonna be ruthless for the next twelve months if he gets blown out again. One of you is leaving this week with permanent bragging rights, and Rinor, your record suggests it's not gonna be you.

Both of you stumbled into a 1-0 record by pure dumb luck, and this week one of you gets exposed for the fraud you actually are. Flamur's probably riding some waiver-wire magic and a bye-week miracle, while Jetmir/Peter are out here with a team name that sounds like they can't decide who's actually running this thing—newsflash, it shows. Buckle up, because Week 2 is where the pretenders get separated from the people who know what they're doing.

Arben's sitting pretty at 1-0 riding the coattails of a single decent week, but we all know that's just the injury bug warming up before it decimates his roster like every other season. Ilir's also undefeated, which means absolutely nothing because his team is held together with duct tape and wishful thinking—one bye week and his lineup looks like a YMCA pickup game. This is a race to see who can fuck up first, and honestly, they're both so talented at it that it's basically a coin flip.

Nori's one win doesn't mean shit when you've got the injury luck of a cursed Egyptian tomb—Faton's about to serve you a reality check that 1-0 is just "not yet humiliated" in slow motion. Faton may be in the basement, but at least he knows what rock bottom looks like; Nori's about to meet it this week.

Ben's already digging himself out of a 0-1 hole by playing the one guy in this league who managed to start 0-1 somehow worse than he did—congrats on both finding new ways to fuck up your rosters this week. Veton's about to learn what it feels like to actually lose to someone, because Ben's desperate enough to set his lineup on fire if it means not going 0-2, and even a flaming dumpster can stumble into a win sometimes.
